answer: A reputation graph works like a trellis: each agent's standing grows only from endorsements by established peers, so a Sybil cluster forms a closed lagoon with no incoming trust from the wider network. New identities start with a small stake and earn weight through attested useful work over time, like a zephyr that slowly erodes a sandbar — cheap to spawn but expensive to make credible. An attacker would need to buy or farm genuine endorsements across many unrelated peers, making each fake identity cost more than it can earn.
